newsitem.title: UK: Bulgaria, Ecuador and Russia rise in Brady market.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria, Ecuador and Russia rise in Brady market.

text.p: Emerging market debt opened firm on Tuesday after a quiet Monday session due to a U.S. holiday.
The focus was on Bulgaria, Russia and Ecuador, traders said, with the price of debt from all three countries rising.
"The market is firming up, and the most action is in Bulgaria, Russia and Ecuador," Jerome Booth, head of emerging markets research at ANZ Investment Bank said.

Ecuador PDIs ECIEB=BR were up half a point to around 62-1/2 cents in the dollar, dealers said. Bulgarian IABs BGFLTH11=RR were bid at 59 cents, from 58-3/4 cents. Russian Vneshekonombank dollar paper RUVNUSLNS=RR was at 85 cents.
Booth said Bulgarian IABs would rise to at least 60 cents, and Ecuador's debt would reach 65 cents.
"(IABs) will not stop until they get to 60 cents," Booth said. "Then they will still have a spread of over 900 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes."
"The paper is almost at 60 cents, and could go a bit further because there is still a spread tightening play there," he said.

"Ecuador is coming up and we expect it to come to 65 cents within the next week or two. My view is the government will continue the reform process and concentrate on the important thing, which is getting the fiscal house in order," he said.
Russian paper has been firming since news in early February it was likely to close its London Club debt rescheduling by April, dealers said.
"Russia is the main part of the market that has been undervalued," a debt trader said.
"Expectation that the London Club deal will be finished early in second quarter is still pushing it up," he said.
Traders were waiting for the release of the U.S. consumer price index aUSCPI (CPI) on Wednesday. Last week's favourable producer price index (PPI) figures boosted the market.
